answers.question: Test Employee at Grand Island was out of dress code on 10-18, no name tag and wrong shirt for the whole shift
answers.content:
Here's what's relevant for a dress code issue at Grand Island:

**Policy basics:**
- Name tags must be worn and visible at all times while working [p.15].
- Buff City Soap shirts can be any plain black, white, or gray t-shirt/long-sleeve under the branded apron, or a branded top — must be clean, free of wrinkles, no patches/rips/holes visible [p.16-17] [p.16].
- Anyone violating the brand's dress code is to be sent home to change into proper attire and may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination [p.15].

**History I have on Test Employee at Grand Island:**
- You told me earlier today about a separate CA for Test Employee at Grand Island — late to open 10-19, documented as a verbal warning, no payroll deduction. That's a different incident (attendance, not dress code).

This 10-18 dress code incident (missing name tag, wrong shirt, whole shift) is a new, separate issue. Since it's not the same conduct as the attendance incident, I'd treat it on its own rather than stack it onto that history, unless you've already talked to this employee about dress code before.

If you want this documented, I can put together a **Coaching Form** or a **Corrective Action Form** for Test Employee — just say which one and tell me to create it (e.g., "create a coaching form for Test Employee"), and the draft card will come up for you to fill in and finalize.
